content.summary: Reference list entries (96–103) from a clinical guideline focusing on early diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction and acute coronary syndrome, evaluation and validation of 0/1-hour algorithms, and comparisons of high-sensitivity cardiac biomarkers (cardiac troponin I, troponin T, and cardiac myosin-binding protein C).

Chiang CH, Chiang CH, Lee GH, Gi W-T, Wu Y-K, Huang S-S, et al. Safety and efficacy of the European Society of Cardiology 0/1-hour algorithm for diagnosis of myocardial infarction: systematic review and meta-analysis. Heart 2020;106:985–991.

Vigen R, Kutscher P, Fernandez F, Yu A, Bertulfo B, Hashim IA, et al. Evaluation of a novel rule-out myocardial infarction protocol incorporating high-sensitivity troponin T in a US hospital. Circulation 2018;138:2061–2063.
Katus H, Ziegler A, Ekinci O, Giannitsis E, Stough WG, Achenbach S, et al. Early diagnosis of acute coronary syndrome. Eur Heart J 2017;38:3049–3055.

genes.context: Mentioned as 'cardiac troponin I' (ref 101) and discussed generically as cardiac troponin in several studies (refs 97, 102, 103) in the context of early diagnosis and assay validation.
'Troponin T' is explicitly referenced (ref 99) and cardiac troponins are compared/used for early diagnosis in other referenced studies (refs 97, 102, 103).

Associated Conditions: Early diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction
genes.context: Ref 102 directly compares 'cardiac myosin-binding protein C' with cardiac troponins for the early diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction.
